subject: Renewal: capacity expansion + token-rate commitment for next term
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@zetacorp.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@zetacorp.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: capacity expansion + token-rate commitment for next term

Hi Aditya,

We're approaching our renewal window and want to formalize the Dedicated capacity increase we discussed on the call. High-level ask: add 10x A100s to our Reserved Pool (bringing total to 30 GPUs), and include a token-rate commitment for the pool during business hours (US) to support a sustained load pattern.

Traffic profile: baseline 90k tokens/sec across the pool (sustained), peak bursts up to ~220k tokens/sec for short windows (1-3 min) during morning ingest. We'd like an addendum that ensures the baseline token rate and a clear remediation/credit if the pool cannot reach it due to platform-side throttling.

Can you share a draft addendum and the pricing delta for the additional GPUs? Also advise on how we should express the SLO (measured at 1-minute intervals vs 5-minute) and any constraints for cold-start or scaling windows.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of ML Platforms
ZetaCorp

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@zetacorp.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: capacity expansion + token-rate commitment for next term

Hi Elena — thanks, this is clear and matches our notes from the renewal call. High level: we can add 10 A100s into a dedicated Reserved Pool and attach a token-rate commitment measured at the pool level.

Proposed measurements:
- Baseline entitlement: 120,000 tokens/sec sustained (pool-level) measured across 5-minute rolling windows during defined business hours (Mon-Fri 7:00-19:00 PT).
- Burst headroom: up to 250,000 tokens/sec for bursts up to 3 minutes; these are best-effort but we will track and report usages.
- SLO: 99.5% of 5-minute windows in the monthly billing period must meet baseline entitlement. If unmet, customer receives service credits computed as a percentage of monthly Dedicated fee (detailed in draft).

Notes/constraints: cold-starts for new models or very large context loads may not meet baseline for short windows — we'll carve out a 10-minute warm-up exemption per model version rollout, and we recommend pinning model versions to minimize variability.

I attached a first-pass addendum and a capacity worksheet with pricing. Monica and Neha are looped for CS/ops and pricing confirmation.

Next steps: Monica to confirm operational monitoring hooks and lead weekly rollout checks; Neha to confirm commercials. If that looks good, we'll route the addendum to legal for final SLA language.

—Aditya
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- We'll expose pool-level telemetry in the Console (tokens/sec, per-route token counts, autoscale events, and queue depth).
- We'll set up a shared Grafana dashboard and an alert that fires if the 5-minute rolling tokens/sec drops below 95% of entitlement for >3 consecutive windows.

Two asks from our ops side:
1) Confirm the business hours definition (we propose Mon-Fri 07:00-19:00 PT as Aditya suggested).
2) Confirm models that will be running on the pool when we perform capacity validation (model ids or pinned versions).

I'll coordinate a 30-min runbook walk-through next week with Elena/Tom to validate alerts and the run-to-fail test.

- Incremental cost for 10x A100s (reserved term, 12 months) = $XXX,XXX/month; this includes the reserved pool, baseline monitoring, and 24/7 priority queueing.

Subject: Re: Renewal: capacity expansion + token-rate commitment for next term

Elena — attaching revised SLO clause (text pasted below) and the exclusion list we propose. Please review and flag any redlines.

Proposed SLO clause (draft language):
"Redwood will provision a Reserved Pool for ZetaCorp sized at 30 A100 GPUs for the contract term. Redwood guarantees a Baseline Token Rate Entitlement of 120,000 tokens per second (tokens/sec) at the pool level, measured using a 5-minute rolling window during Customer Business Hours (Mon-Fri 07:00-19:00 PT). Platform-induced throttling or capacity exhaustion that causes a 5-minute window to fall below the Baseline Entitlement will be considered a breach for that window. Monthly SLO compliance is defined as the percentage of 5-minute windows in the month that meet the Baseline Entitlement. Remedies: if Monthly SLO compliance falls below 99.5%, Customer will receive service credits as defined in Schedule A (tiered credit scheme based on severity)."

Exclusions (non-exhaustive):
- Customer software or model behaviors that generate pathological tail traffic (as determined by mutual investigation).
- Planned maintenance windows (minimum 72-hour advance notice) and emergency maintenance.
- Model version rollouts with less than 10 minutes of warm-up time after pinning.

Please confirm and I'll incorporate into the addendum PDF for signature.

—Marissa
Legal Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
